Alex: FYI noticed a spike in OOMs on nightly for the medium-latency repro (mostly long-prefix, KV-heavy requests). Lots of them come from the continuous-batcher path when kernel X is selected. :grimacing:
Tina: ugh. any flamegraph or perf numbers?
Alex: quick snapshot from the profiling run:
```
sample_count: 1200
avg_latency_ms: 48.3
p99_latency_ms: 220
kv_cache_evictions/sec: 8.7
batch_tokens_mean: 248
kernel_choice: kernel_x (selected 84% of runs)
memory_headroom_mb: 210 -> frequently drops under 128 before eviction spike
```
Alex: the interesting bit is kernel_x gives good raw throughput for short sequences but its working-set (KV mapping / temp buffers) is ~2.2x compared to kernel_y for these long-prefix cases.
Jorge: did the batch formation change recently? we had a tweak to extend the token budget window last week.
Alex: yes — token-budget target bumped from 300 -> 400 for the front window. the admission logic now tries to favor larger batches which seems to push the working set over the safe threshold when kv cache is dense.
Maya: so two factors: larger batches + kernel that uses larger ephemeral memory. combined -> OOM. makes sense.
Tina: is the scheduler aware of KV cache occupancy when forming batches? currently it reads a single `memory_headroom` value but doesn't account for per-kv-fragment spikes.
Jorge: correct. we aggregate per-GPU headroom and apply a simple min-threshold gating. doesn't track active-kv-fragments per-request.
Alex: perf-bot posted a detailed trace into /perf/5123 if you want to see allocation heatmaps. perf-bot: <link> :eyes:
perf-bot: Allocation heatmap attached: https://internal/perf/5123/heatmap.png (auto-upload)
Maya: proposal: add a lightweight kv-occupancy hint on request metadata (approx KV footprint in tokens -> estimate MB) and have batcher compute a conservative sum when admitting. if sum > headroom*0.8 then fall back to kernel_y or reduce token budget.
Tina: +1. also suggest we prefer kernel_y when estimated KV footprint per-batch > threshold. fallback path should maintain latency SLOs by shrinking token budget rather than full reject.
Jorge: implementation details: two parts — (1) estimator (tiny table lookup: tokens -> mb) and (2) admission change: compute estimated_batch_kv_mb = sum(estimator(req.tokens)) and compare to dynamic_headroom. if > gate -> try kernel_y with reduced budget; if still > gate -> split batch.
Alex: splitting batch is the safest; prefer in-order split to avoid changing latency profile too much. note: splitting can increase overall GPU work but keeps system stable.
Maya: can we avoid adding heavy logic in hot path? estimator must be O(1) and cheap. maybe precompute per-request hint at front of pipeline and carry it as a small int in the request header.
Tina: agree. also add a lightweight metric and alert for admission fallback rate so we can monitor regressions.
Alex: action items:
- Jorge: prototype estimator + admission hook (PR by EOD Wed)
- Maya: run perf comparison kernel_x vs kernel_y on traced heavy-kv requests and publish numbers (by Tue)
- Tina: add alert for fallback_rate and KV-eviction/sec (by Fri)
- Alex: run a canary (5% traffic) with new gating once Jorge's PR lands
Jorge: noted, will start on estimator.
Maya: will attach the kernel memory profiles in the PR.
Tina: thanks. if we can avoid a full rollback this week that'd be ideal :relieved:
Alex: agreed. last note — for telemetry we should emit the estimated_batch_kv_mb and chosen_kernel in traces so we can correlate fallbacks with real OOMs.
perf-bot: scheduled nightly regression job to include these new traces after PR merge. :white_check_mark:
Alex: awesome. ping me if you hit blockers.
